key_insight: This paper shows how vision-language model (VLM) agents can help robots learn new tasks from context at deployment time, instead of relying only on fixed pretraining or large demo datasets. The core idea is to make robot behavior more adaptable to unfamiliar environments using the reasoning and multimodal understanding of modern VLMs.
problem_solved: Robots usually struggle to generalize to new tasks, objects, and environments because they cannot learn effectively from a small amount of context during deployment. This work targets the challenge of in-context learning for robotics, where a robot must adapt without requiring exhaustive task-specific demonstrations.
method: Use a VLM agent as a high-level reasoning and perception module to interpret the scene, task instructions, and context.
Translate contextual observations into actionable robot decisions, enabling adaptation to novel situations at test time.
Leverage the agentic capabilities of commercial VLMs to support flexible, on-the-fly policy selection rather than a fully fixed robot policy.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this points toward a more practical path for general-purpose robotics: systems that can adapt online with minimal task-specific data. It suggests VLM-based agents may reduce the need for massive robot demonstration datasets and improve real-world robustness.

paper_title: In-Context Robot Learning with VLM Agents
paper_authors: Dongzhou Cheng, Taoran Yi, Ye Fang, Xingwu Zhang, Fan Feng
